title: After Byzantium: imperial endings and inheritance
summary: Ottoman emergence occurred amid shifting frontier relations and weakening older arrangements. Expansion depended not only on military capability but also on organizing newly incorporated populations, territories and social relationships.

blocks.text: Ottoman emergence occurred amid shifting frontier relations and weakening older arrangements. Expansion depended not only on military capability but also on organizing newly incorporated populations, territories and social relationships.

The end of the Byzantine political center did not simultaneously terminate all its cities, religious life, knowledge and political memory. Different inheritances could enter different settings, where later people preserved, changed or reinterpreted them.

blocks.caption: Ottoman Expansion · Context illustration; historical interpretation is in the text.

blocks.text: Succession therefore requires several levels of observation. Sovereignty could disappear while religious communities continued. Institutions could be replaced while knowledge and urban functions survived differently. One word such as disappearance cannot describe all these changes.

Conversely, surviving legacies do not erase conquest and rupture. Inheritance includes preservation, loss and the reorganization of power. Distinguishing them explains how an empire's influence can remain present within a world that no longer contains the same empire.
